summary.headline: GNG Electronics Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR624.8 crore with gross margin up 515 bps to 25.1%; FY27 top-line guidance raised to 40%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR624.8 crore versus INR439.9 crore a year earlier, with India up about 45% and international up about 40%. Gross margin expanded 515 bps YoY to 25.1%, and H1 revenue reached INR1,037 crore (up 38%) with gross margin of 24.9%. Management raised FY27 guidance to 40% revenue growth and 150 bps net margin expansion over FY26 (from 30% and 100 bps). Management attributed part of the margin gain (125-150 bps) to inventory bought at older prices, and said inventory and receivables will stay elevated for at least the next two quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: India revenue grew about 45% YoY in Q2 FY27, with management citing stronger performance from key channel partners.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International revenue grew about 40% YoY in Q2 FY27; Electronics Bazaar now supplies 55 countries, up from 49 at end of Q1.

segments.name: Laptops vs others
segments.commentary: Laptops and others continue to be about 78-80% of revenue, with laptop ASP up about 11% YoY in H1 on better realisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 40% YoY (raised from 30%).
FY27 net profit margin expected to expand about 150 bps over FY26 (raised from 75-100 bps); FY26 base is about 7% net margin per analyst.
FY27 effective tax rate assumed at 14-16%.
Net debt expected to stay broadly flat at around INR427 crore through FY27 end; funding of inventory described as substantially accruals-driven.
No FY28 guidance given at this stage; management said it would revisit as the market evolves.
Inventory expected to stay elevated for at least the next two quarters; long-run target about 90 days of projected sales in around two years.
capex_capacity: India workspace roughly doubled around two to three quarters before the call; UAE facilities increased from 3-4 to about 8.
H1 FY27 volume about 3.75 lakh units; management says full-year volume will still be below 1 million, implying about 40-50% capacity utilisation.
Teammates grew to 2,811 (Sept 2026) from 2,420; sales and marketing headcount rose from about 196 to 233 in one quarter.
Hiring engineering, leadership and sales talent in India, international markets, Singapore and Vietnam for Asia Pacific expansion.
demand_pricing: IDC: global PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY in the September 2026 quarter (62.7 million vs 78.5 million); IDC expects a similar decline in the December quarter and a 11.3% decline for CY2026.

New laptop price in India reportedly moved from INR35,000-40,000 a year ago to INR65,000-72,000; management says a new computer that cost INR100 is now INR180, and its refurbished product could go to about INR54 (from about INR30).
Management says it can raise its refurbished pricing from about 30% to 35-45% of new device price, while noting sourcing costs are rising but trailing new-device price moves.
Receivable days rose modestly; management says normal channel credit is 60-90 days and receivables run at about 40-45 days.
Inventory sourced in bulk from large banks and corporates; management says some of it was bought at older prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin expansion sustainable, and what is the revised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, citing a permanent reset in new-device prices and brand-led pricing power; FY27 top-line guidance raised to about 40% and net margin guidance to about 150 bps expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from inventory gains versus underlying pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the 400-500 bps quarterly margin expansion, management attributed about 125-150 bps to strategic inventory purchases; the rest was pricing and realisation. It expects similar inventory benefit from recent purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the comfortable debt level and inventory steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR427 crore, expected to remain similar through FY27. Inventory is expected to normalise to about 90 days of projected sales in around two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate higher and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 effective tax rate about 18% versus 10.6% in FY26 as India profitability rose; FY27 tax rate assumed at 14-16%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost growing faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hiring ahead of growth in engineering, sales, leadership and corporate roles, with sales and marketing headcount up from about 196 to 233 in one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity headroom and FY27 debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is well placed; utilisation is about 40-50% and volumes will remain below 1 million units. Net debt is expected to stay around INR427 crore with no significant debt increase needed.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to demand and prices if memory prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pre-AI growth exceeded 30% YoY over the previous three years, the model works in both cycles, and inventory bought at old prices gives a cushion.

risks_watch: Inventory build (elevated for at least two quarters) keeps working capital and net debt under pressure; receivable days have risen.
Margin guidance relies partly on inventory gains (125-150 bps of expansion), which may not persist if memory prices fall.
Rising employee cost ahead of revenue; tax rate rising from about 10.6% to 14-16%.
Demand sensitivity to memory price trajectory and to a possible slowdown in new-PC demand, as stated by IDC.
Sourcing costs are rising, though trailing new-device price increases; supply of used equipment may shrink as corporates extend leases.
Management declined to give FY28 guidance; watch for any update in next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pricing and guidance upgrades, with management repeatedly describing the company as underpromising and overdelivering. Answers on the inventory build, tax rate and FY28 were more hedged, relying on qualitative explanations rather than detailed figures.
key_quotes: We are solving the trust issue and trust is a huge margin lever.
Elevated memory prices are a near-term catalyst for us. They are not the foundation of our business.
We have always been on the side of caution, always try to underpromise and overdeliver.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 40% (from 30%) with Q2 revenue up 42% YoY and H1 up 38%, but utilisation is only ~40-50% and the margin tailwind is partly from older-priced inventory, so backing is partial rather than clear capacity or order-book support.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose 515 bps YoY to 25.1% in Q2 and FY27 net margin guided up about 150 bps, with management citing a permanent reset in new-device prices, though 125-150 bps of the quarterly gain came from older-priced inventory that may not persist.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 40-50% with full-year volume still below 1 million units, and India workspace and UAE facilities were already expanded before the call, so no new capacity is needed in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume was about 2,25,000 units, up about 30% YoY, and H1 reached about 3,74,000 units, with international revenue up about 40% and Electronics Bazaar now supplying 55 countries (up from 49).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: With utilisation at about 45% and existing capacity expanded, there is no sign of a new capex plan; management said Net debt stays flat at about INR427 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue is up 38% and FY27 growth guide was already raised to 40% from 30%, but IDC's expected 11.3% CY2026 PC decline and the reliance on inventory gains limit further upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Roughly 125-150 bps of the 150 bps FY27 margin guide relies on older-priced inventory, and IDC expects PC shipments to fall 20.1% YoY in Sept 2026 quarter and a similar decline in Dec quarter, so a memory-price reversal could cut the margin guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launch was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Inventory and receivables stay elevated
rows.why: Management said inventory and receivables will stay elevated for at least two quarters, with receivables at about 40-45 days and inventory targeted at about 90 days of sales in around two years.

rows.label: Net debt held flat at about INR427 crore
rows.why: Net debt was about INR427 crore at end Q2 (up from INR406 crore at Q1) and is guided to stay similar, with inventory funding described as substantially accruals-driven.

rows.label: Refurbished device pricing reset
rows.why: Management says it can raise refurbished pricing from about 30% to 35-45% of new device price, while laptop ASP rose to about INR31,000 from INR28,000 YoY, but this depends on sourcing costs and memory prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and the raised FY27 guidance, but hedged on the inventory-driven margin gain, the rise in tax rate and FY28; analysts pressed on how much of the margin is sustainable versus inventory gains.
